originality.rationale: The unconstrained Chebyshev residual optimum covers the single budget t=t_2, and classical degree-two real-axis stability polynomials cover the kappa>=2 safe-horizon endpoint; neither supplies the full prescribed-sum minimax family or the 1<kappa<2 safe-time cutoff. Separate published published-finding corpus results impose stagewise safety or different methods. The classical Zolotarev first problem fixes leading coefficients, not a prescribed residual value and first derivative. Actual searches and full-text method sections were compared by hypotheses and implication; an unindexed classical equivalent remains possible.

value.rationale: Two-step time partitioning for spectral diffusion is a natural smallest variable-grid optimization. An externally fixed total duration is a nontrivial constraint absent from unconstrained Chebyshev tuning. The exact continuum robust phase diagram and kappa-dependent maximal nonexpansion duration explain when final-step stabilization permits transiently expansive stages; the comparison with equal partition is sharp and practical. The result makes no unsupported accuracy claim.
